decision: Treat the PDF as a search-loop design, not a sufficient production safety proof

decision: Use mining, adaptive promotion, and a one-use sealed final audit
alternatives: Reuse one held-out set every round
evidence: The paper evaluates every candidate on held-out data, making that set adaptive; independent review agreed
reversibility: Schema and fixtures can change before implementation

decision: Keep Host and Store as sole durable authority
alternatives: External Python driver; Harbor authority; new daemon
evidence: Repository mapping shows Host owns sessions/tools and Store owns protected state, events, receipts, and fencing

decision: Evolve content-addressed declarative behavior manifests only
evidence: Threat analysis and all three architecture candidates converged on a compiled immutable authority layer
reversibility: Editable allowlist can narrow; expansion requires a new reviewed version

decision: Require case-level paired inference, frozen gates, full composite re-test, and tri-state verdicts
alternatives: Raw score deltas; attempt-level inference; infer merged safety
evidence: Paper limitations, repository CheckStatus precedent, and cross-judge corrections
reversibility: Estimator is versioned and replaceable only prospectively

decision: Select architecture Candidate 2 and graft sealed evidence, audit, supersession, fencing, and no-subset-search rules

alternatives: One large implementation; 8 or 12 broad phases
evidence: Store migration, artifact ACLs, Host binding, caller migration, evidence, statistics, activation, recovery, and operator surfaces need independently verifiable revisions
reversibility: Adjacent phases may merge only after tests prove the boundary is unnecessary

decision: Do not enable registry writes until suite partitions, power/noise policy, sealed ACLs, and provider reconciliation are proven
alternatives: Pick thresholds and fixtures during coding
evidence: Open decisions in overview; no runtime implementation evidence exists yet

decision: Make evaluation cohorts and their query/error ledgers Store-global across campaigns
alternatives: Reset ledgers for each campaign; reuse a held-out set
evidence: Adversarial statistical review found cross-campaign reuse would evade multiplicity and audit retirement
reversibility: New non-overlapping cohorts may be committed prospectively

decision: Represent mining, adaptive promotion, and final audit as non-interchangeable dataset capabilities
evidence: Information-flow review found a generic type would permit confirmation evidence to feed search
reversibility: New roles require a prospective protocol version

decision: Migrate Store schema and artifact visibility before session binding or sealed evidence writes
alternatives: Bind first; rely on raw artifact digests
evidence: Repository review found schema v1 event-kind constraints and public raw artifact reads incompatible with the planned invariants
reversibility: Migration must preserve existing aggregates and artifacts

decision: Classify valid evaluator rejection, attributable crash, budget exhaustion, and protocol timeout as behavioral failure; reserve unknown for unverifiable infrastructure
alternatives: Treat every crash or timeout as inconclusive
evidence: Adversarial review found the broad unknown category lets weak candidates hide failures
reversibility: Taxonomy is frozen per evaluation protocol

decision: Do not promise exactly-once external execution or payment
evidence: Current native Docker and provider interfaces cannot always recover a completed external result after Host death; safe version 1 behavior is inspect/collect/fence where supported, otherwise terminal unknown with conservative debit

decision: Migrate interactive session authority to the durable Host independently of Harbor
alternatives: Wait for Harbor; keep client-assembled privileged instructions
evidence: Repository inspection shows the Host already owns durable sessions and Harbor is not required for admission or binding
reversibility: Harbor may later implement the same transport contract

decision: Treat plan integrity and implementation evidence as separate verdicts
alternatives: Claim runtime readiness from a reviewed design
evidence: Twenty plan artifacts, fifteen phase structures, relative links, TSV shape, exact test-target commands, path hygiene, and whitespace were checked; no production code or Rust tests were run
reversibility: Implementation and production enablement remain INCONCLUSIVE until their phase gates pass
